why: The paper's contribution IS the ctsfeatures R package, and that package is released on CRAN with all four datasets used by the claims (GeneticSequences, SyntheticData1, SyntheticData3) bundled, plus the exact functions the target claim needs (total_correlation, marginal_probabilities, outlier_score, dist/colSums/boxplot). No training, no weights, no missing configs: the target C1 is a deterministic ~1-minute R script over 32 packaged sequences. The only work is installing R + the CRAN package on this machine, which is a small environment step, not a rebuild.
entrypoints: R: library(ctsfeatures); data(GeneticSequences); features <- cbind(total_correlation(GeneticSequences$data, categories=factor(c('a','g','c','t')), features=TRUE), marginal_probabilities(GeneticSequences$data, categories=factor(c('a','g','c','t')))); dist_db <- as.matrix(dist(features)); outlier_score <- colSums(dist_db); boxplot(outlier_score, range=1); order(outlier_score, decreasing=TRUE)[1:2]
R (secondary claims): caret::train(method='knn'/'rf', trControl=trainControl(method='LOOCV')) on cbind(gini_index(...), cramers_vi(lag=1, ...))
missing_artifacts: No standalone author analysis script: the paper's code is inline in the article/vignette, so a short driver script must be assembled from the printed snippets (verbatim, given in the claim contract)
R runtime is not listed among installed tooling (only Python 3.12.10 is); R must be installed if absent
blockers_seen: Machine is Windows 11 with no GPU and Python-based tooling; the experiment is R-only, so an R installation and CRAN binary download are prerequisites

ctsfeatures depends on a chain of CRAN packages (Rcpp, ggplot2, caret, forecast-family deps for the classification examples); binary install on Windows is straightforward but pulls ~50-100 MB of dependencies

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: ~8-15 min total: ~5 min R install + CRAN binary package and dependency download, <10 s to load GeneticSequences and compute the dB distance matrix, outlier scores and boxplot; C2/C3/C4 add ~1-2 min (caret LOOCV on 32 series is near-instant; a single random-forest LOOCV fit is seconds)

compute.basis: A single 32x32 distance matrix and colSums on the packaged GeneticSequences data (sub-second), plus a one-time R + ctsfeatures CRAN binary install that dominates the wall clock; caret kNN/RF LOOCV over 32 two-feature rows adds under two minutes.
